question: What will the Antarctic sea ice extent be on September 3, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Antarctic sea ice extent for 2026-09-03 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I found no prediction market or expert forecast for this exact number. Excluding today's provisional reading, recent daily values put the Antarctic extent at about 15.95 to 16.03 million km² (Mkm²), lower than every recent year except 2023. Over the last five years, the gain from August 13 to September 3 ranged from +0.50 to +1.70 Mkm², with a mean of about +0.98.

Note: the NSIDC file I fetched today also contains data after August 13, 2026. I only asked for and only report rows up to 2026-08-13. I also left out search results published after that date, including Copernicus' August summary, NASA's maximum announcement and Zack Labe's September updates.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-13: The question resolves on NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4, `S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv`, in Mkm². [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Latest values in the file:
  - Aug 4: 16.369, the recent peak
  - Aug 8: 16.292
  - Aug 9: 16.085
  - Aug 10: 15.975
  - Aug 11: 15.955
  - Aug 12: 15.971
  - Aug 13: 16.030 (same-day values are provisional and may not have been posted yet when forecasts close)
- Late July values:
  - Jul 25: 15.604
  - Jul 31: 16.009
  - Aug 1: 16.222

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The resolving number is three weeks away.
- 2026-08-04 to 08-11: extent fell by about 0.41 Mkm² after the Aug 4 peak, which stalled growth. A forum post reported the same drop, and it matches the CSV. [Lemmy](https://lemmy.manganiello.tech/post/531651/680421)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Early Aug 2026: The Met Office briefing put Antarctic extent at 16.65 Mkm² on 2 August, the 4th lowest for that date. It uses a different dataset, so the level differs from NSIDC's. [Met Office Aug briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- Early Aug 2026: July 2026 averaged 15.39 to 15.4 Mkm², the 5th lowest July, about 6.4% below the 1991-2020 average. Ice was below average in most sectors except the Amundsen Sea. [Met Office July](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic-and-antarctic-sea-ice-july-2026), [Copernicus July](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-july-2026)
- 2026-02-26: The annual minimum was 2.58 Mkm², higher than in recent years. [theweather.net](https://www.theweather.net/news/trending/good-news-antarctic-sea-ice-has-melted-slightly-less-this-year.html)
- Zack Labe's NSIDC-based charts: [zacklabe.com](https://zacklabe.com/antarctic-sea-ice-extentconcentration/)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality (NSIDC v4 daily, Mkm²)

| Year | Aug 13 | Sep 3 | Change | Annual max (daily value, date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 18.048 | 18.612 | +0.56 | 18.893, Aug 30 |
| 2022 | 16.854 | 17.779 | +0.93 | 18.276, Sep 13 |
| 2023 | 15.150 | 16.852 | +1.70 | 17.109, Sep 7 |
| 2024 | 16.539 | 17.034 | +0.50 | 17.283, Sep 15 |
| 2025 | 16.316 | 17.530 | +1.21 | 17.854, Sep 15 |

- The 5-year gain from Aug 13 to Sep 3 has a mean of about +0.98 and a range of +0.50 to +1.70, a spread of about 1.2 Mkm².
- 2026 is running below 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 by about 0.3 to 2.0 Mkm², and about 0.9 above 2023.
- Simple arithmetic: 16.03 plus the historical gains gives about 16.5 to 17.7, centred near 17.0. This is just a calculation from the table, not a forecast.
- In all five years, the Sep 3 value was within about 0.3 to 0.4 of the annual maximum, or right at it.
- Day-to-day swings of 0.1 to 0.2 Mkm² are common, such as the -0.21 on Aug 8 to 9, 2026. Short storm-driven drops or jumps can move a single day's value noticeably.
- The 2021 to 2025 values above came from asking a summarising tool about sections of the CSV. They agree with known seasonal patterns but are worth spot-checking in the raw file.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market, and no published expert forecast, for Antarctic extent on Sep 3, 2026.
- I also found no NSIDC Antarctic outlook. NSIDC does not normally issue predictions for the Antarctic maximum.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Daily NSIDC updates continue, and the early-September NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News post will come out before resolution. Copernicus and Met Office monthly summaries come out in early September.
- The weather matters most here: Southern Ocean winds and storms, plus low ice in the Indian Ocean sector and the Amundsen Sea, can compress or spread the ice edge. I found no official short-range or seasonal outlook for Antarctic sea ice covering August 13 to September 3.
- The annual maximum usually falls between late August and mid-September (dates for 2021 to 2025 are in the table above), so September 3 is near the seasonal plateau.
